page: Amazon Web Services hpc7g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance within the High Performance Computing family, managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 64 physical cores and 64 vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture operating at 2.6 GHz, without simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and no discrete GPUs are present. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute efficiency. In Geekbench multi-core testing, the instance reaches the top 10% tier with a score of 20607.0, alongside top-tier Clang compilation performance. Stress-ng multi-core testing places in the top 25% with 97889.61, while single-core metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the average tier. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high throughput, with PassMark memory scoring in the top 10% and uncached large-block read bandwidth achieving 276.16 GB/sec. The absence of hyperthreading eliminates thread contention, delivering consistent parallel throughput per physical core at a compute-dense resource ratio.

Given the 200 Gbps networking capacity and 64 dedicated physical ARM cores, the hpc7g.16xlarge is suited for tightly coupled high-performance computing, distributed scientific simulations, large code compilation pipelines, and parallel batch processing tasks that rely on external storage arrays.

Multi-core performance is strong, registering top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core and Clang software compilation benchmarks, supported by high memory throughput reaching 276.16 GB/sec on large read operations. Single-thread execution ranks in the average tier, reflecting its emphasis on dense physical core parallelization over single-thread burst frequencies. With dedicated Nitro virtualization and high network interconnect capacity, this server is suitable for tightly coupled distributed simulations, scientific computing, parallel Clang builds, and multi-node HPC clusters relying on network-attached storage.
